(** Assertion *)
assert(flag:Boolean): () =
    if NOT flag then
        fail("Assertion failed!")
    end

assert(flag: Boolean, failMsg: String): () =
    if NOT flag then
        fail(failMsg)
    end

assert(x:Any, y:Any, failMsg: Any...): () =
    if x =/= y then
        xs = typecase x of
                 x':Object => x'.asDebugString
                 else => "" x
             end
        ys = typecase y of
                 y':Object => y'.asDebugString
                 else => "" y
             end
        msg = xs " =/= " ys "; " (BIG || failMsg)  (* use || here instead of loose juxt *)
        fail(msg)
    end

component VectorMatrixCastsWalk

vectorOps[\T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }\](x: T, y: T, n0: T, name: String): () = do
    u = vector[\T,2\]()
    u[0] := x
    u[1] := y
    w = vector[\T,2\](y)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](w), true, name, ": vector(v) answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, vector")
    assert(w[0], y, name, ": vector(v) fills; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, vector")
    assert(w[1], y, name, ": vector(v) fills; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, vector")

    s = u + w
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](s), true, name, ": u + w answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")
    assert(instanceOf[\T\](s[0]), true, name, ": u + w holds the element type; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")
    assert(s[0], x + y, name, ": (u + w)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")
    assert(s[1], y + y, name, ": (u + w)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")

    d = u - w
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](d), true, name, ": u - w answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -")
    assert(d[0], x - y, name, ": (u - w)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -")
    assert(d[1], y - y, name, ": (u - w)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -")

    n = -(vector[\T,2\](n0))
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](n), true, name, ": unary minus answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -(self)")
    assert(n[0], -n0, name, ": (-v)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -(self)")
    assert(n[1], -n0, name, ": (-v)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -(self)")

    c = u.scale(y)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](c), true, name, ": scale answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, scale")
    assert(c[0], y x, name, ": u.scale(y)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, scale")
    assert(c[1], y y, name, ": u.scale(y)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, scale")

    p = u.pmul(w)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](p), true, name, ": pmul answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, pmul")
    assert(p[0], x y, name, ": u.pmul(w)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, pmul")
    assert(p[1], y y, name, ": u.pmul(w)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, pmul")

    f = vector[\T,2\]().fill(x)

    assert(f[0], x, name, ": fill(x)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")
    assert(f[1], x, name, ": fill(x)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")

    t = vector[\T,2\]().tabulate(fn (i: ZZ32): T => if i = 0 then y else x end)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](t), true, name, ": tabulate answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")
    assert(t[0], y, name, ": tabulate(f)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")
    assert(t[1], x, name, ": tabulate(f)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")

    tv = tabulatedVector[\T,2\](fn (i: ZZ32): T => if i = 0 then x else y end)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](tv), true, name, ": tabulatedVector answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, tabulatedVector")
    assert(tv[0], x, name, ": tabulatedVector(f)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, tabulatedVector")
    assert(tv[1], y, name, ": tabulatedVector(f)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, tabulatedVector")

(* The vector and matrix operations, factories, columns and rows answer their declared array types with the right elements at each of the eight number types. *)
component VectorMatrixCastsWalk
export Executable

vectorOps[\T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }\](x: T, y: T, n0: T, name: String): () = do
    u = vector[\T,2\]()
    u[0] := x
    u[1] := y
    w = vector[\T,2\](y)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](w), true, name, ": vector(v) answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, vector")
    assert(w[0], y, name, ": vector(v) fills; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, vector")
    assert(w[1], y, name, ": vector(v) fills; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, vector")

    s = u + w
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](s), true, name, ": u + w answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")
    assert(instanceOf[\T\](s[0]), true, name, ": u + w holds the element type; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")
    assert(s[0], x + y, name, ": (u + w)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")
    assert(s[1], y + y, name, ": (u + w)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr +")

    d = u - w
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](d), true, name, ": u - w answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -")
    assert(d[0], x - y, name, ": (u - w)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -")
    assert(d[1], y - y, name, ": (u - w)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -")

    n = -(vector[\T,2\](n0))
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](n), true, name, ": unary minus answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -(self)")
    assert(n[0], -n0, name, ": (-v)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -(self)")
    assert(n[1], -n0, name, ": (-v)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, opr -(self)")

    c = u.scale(y)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](c), true, name, ": scale answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, scale")
    assert(c[0], y x, name, ": u.scale(y)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, scale")
    assert(c[1], y y, name, ": u.scale(y)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, scale")

    p = u.pmul(w)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](p), true, name, ": pmul answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, pmul")
    assert(p[0], x y, name, ": u.pmul(w)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, pmul")
    assert(p[1], y y, name, ": u.pmul(w)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector, pmul")

    f = vector[\T,2\]().fill(x)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](f), true, name, ": fill answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")
    assert(f[0], x, name, ": fill(x)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")
    assert(f[1], x, name, ": fill(x)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")

    t = vector[\T,2\]().tabulate(fn (i: ZZ32): T => if i = 0 then y else x end)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](t), true, name, ": tabulate answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")
    assert(t[0], y, name, ": tabulate(f)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")
    assert(t[1], x, name, ": tabulate(f)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Vector")

    tv = tabulatedVector[\T,2\](fn (i: ZZ32): T => if i = 0 then x else y end)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](tv), true, name, ": tabulatedVector answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, tabulatedVector")
    assert(tv[0], x, name, ": tabulatedVector(f)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, tabulatedVector")
    assert(tv[1], y, name, ": tabulatedVector(f)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, tabulatedVector")
  end

matrixOps[\T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }\](x: T, y: T, z: T, n0: T, name: String): () = do
    m = matrix[\T,2,2\]()
    m[0,0] := x
    m[0,1] := y
    m[1,0] := z
    m[1,1] := x
    k = matrix[\T,2,2\](y)
    assert(instanceOf[\Matrix[\T,2,2\]\](k), true, name, ": matrix(v) answers a Matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, matrix")
    assert(k[0,0], y, name, ": matrix(v) puts v on the diagonal; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, matrix")
    assert(k[0,1], x.zero, name, ": matrix(v) puts zero off the diagonal; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, matrix")
    assert(k[1,1], y, name, ": matrix(v) puts v on the diagonal; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, matrix")

    s = m + k
    assert(instanceOf[\Matrix[\T,2,2\]\](s), true, name, ": m + k answers a Matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr +")

    assert(s[0,0], x + y, name, ": (m + k)[0,0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr +")
    assert(s[1,0], z, name, ": (m + k)[1,0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr +")

    d = m - k
    assert(instanceOf[\Matrix[\T,2,2\]\](d), true, name, ": m - k answers a Matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr -")
    assert(d[0,0], x - y, name, ": (m - k)[0,0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr -")
    assert(d[0,1], y, name, ": (m - k)[0,1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr -")

    n = -(matrix[\T,2,2\]().fill(n0))
    assert(instanceOf[\Matrix[\T,2,2\]\](n), true, name, ": unary minus answers a Matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr -(self)")
    assert(n[0,1], -n0, name, ": (-m)[0,1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr -(self)")
    assert(n[1,1], -n0, name, ": (-m)[1,1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr -(self)")

    c = m.scale(y)
    assert(instanceOf[\Matrix[\T,2,2\]\](c), true, name, ": scale answers a Matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, scale")

    assert(c[1,0], y z, name, ": m.scale(y)[1,0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, scale")

    f = matrix[\T,2,2\]().fill(z)

    assert(f[1,1], z, name, ": fill(z)[1,1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix")

    t = matrix[\T,2,2\]().tabulate(fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): T => if i = j then x else z end)
    assert(instanceOf[\Matrix[\T,2,2\]\](t), true, name, ": tabulate answers a Matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix")
    assert(t[0,0], x, name, ": tabulate(f)[0,0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix")
    assert(t[0,1], z, name, ": tabulate(f)[0,1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix")

    u = vector[\T,2\]()
    u[0] := x
    u[1] := y
    r = m.rmul(u)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](r), true, name, ": rmul answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, rmul")
    assert(r[0], x x + y y, name, ": m.rmul(u)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, rmul")
    assert(r[1], z x + x y, name, ": m.rmul(u)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, rmul")
    l = m.lmul(u)
    assert(instanceOf[\Vector[\T,2\]\](l), true, name, ": lmul answers a Vector; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, lmul")
    assert(l[0], x x + y z, name, ": m.lmul(u)[0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, lmul")
    assert(l[1], x y + y x, name, ": m.lmul(u)[1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, lmul")

    tm = m.t()
    assert(instanceOf[\TransposedMatrix[\T,2,2\]\](tm), true, name, ": t() answers a transposed matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, t")
    ts = tm + k
    assert(instanceOf[\Matrix[\T,2,2\]\](ts), true, name, ": a transposed matrix's + answers a Matrix; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr +")
    assert(ts[0,1], z, name, ": (m.t() + k)[0,1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr +")
    assert(ts[1,0], y, name, ": (m.t() + k)[1,0]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr +")
    assert(ts[1,1], x + y, name, ": (m.t() + k)[1,1]; Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, trait Matrix, opr +")
  end

slices[\T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }\](x: T, y: T, z: T, name: String): () = do

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# compare-walk.py <base harness output> <new harness output>: two runs of harness-one.sh over the same
# test files, compared test by test (the harness shuffles their order), with the masks of the
# fortress-repo skill's gate.md, "Comparing with an earlier run". Written for the array-sites probe.
import sys, re, collections
def blocks(p):
    b = collections.OrderedDict(); cur = None
    for l in open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        m = re.match(r"^\. interpret \S*/tests/(\S+)", l)
        if m: cur = m.group(1); b[cur] = []; continue
        if cur is None: continue
        if l.startswith(("OK (", "exit=", "EXIT=", "Time:", "FAILURES")): cur = None; continue
        l = re.sub(r"Operation took \d+ ?ms", "Operation took Nms", l)
        l = re.sub(r"OK \(time = \d+ms\)", "OK (time = Nms)", l)
        l = re.sub(r"@[0-9a-f]{4,}", "@HASH", l)
        l = re.sub(r"(FortressLibrary\.fs[si]):\d+(:\d+)?(-\d+(:\d+)?)?", r"\1:L", l)
        b[cur].append(l.rstrip("\n"))
    return b
a, n = blocks(sys.argv[1]), blocks(sys.argv[2])
print("tests: base %d, new %d" % (len(a), len(n)))
same = 0
for t in sorted(set(a) | set(n)):
    if a.get(t) == n.get(t): same += 1; continue
    if sorted(a.get(t, [])) == sorted(n.get(t, [])):
        print("ORDER ONLY", t); same += 1; continue
    print("DIFFERS", t)
    import difflib
    for d in difflib.unified_diff(a.get(t, []), n.get(t, []), lineterm="", n=0): print("   ", d[:200])
print("equal after masks:", same, "of", len(set(a) | set(n)))
print("verdict lines base:", [l for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if l.startswith(("OK (", "FAILURES", "Tests run"))])
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# compare-sites.py <before.tsv> <after.tsv>: two per-site lists of the distance stage (the landed
# explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv, or errors.py's errors.tsv in a run's scratch folder),
# compared site by site with line numbers masked, and the two export errors entry by entry. Written for
# the array-sites probe (REPORT.md beside it).
import sys, re, collections
def rows(p):
    out = []
    for l in open(p, encoding="utf-8"):
        if l.startswith("#") or not l.strip(): continue
        c = l.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        out.append(c)
    return out
def mask(s): return re.sub(r"(\.fs[si]):\d+([:.]\d+)?(-\d+(:\d+)?)?", r"\1:L", s)
def key(c):
    kind, loc, msg = c[0], c[5], c[6]
    if kind == "export":
        return (kind, mask(loc), mask(msg.split(":")[0]))
    return (kind, mask(loc), mask(msg))
def entries(msg):
    m = re.search(r"\{(.*)\}\s*$", msg)
    if not m: return []
    body = m.group(1)
    # split on top-level ", " that start an entry: missing declarations end in "at FILE:pos"
    if "Missing declarations" in msg:

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

# Source this in every shell that runs Fortress:  source explorations/experiment/env.sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=1
# bin/fortress defaults to -Xmx256m (gap ledger row 67); the checks at 4 threads override FORTRESS_THREADS on the command line
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m"
# every grammar-importing run leaves a 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory behind (RatsUtil.getTempDir); 723 of them filled the disk allowance on 2026-09-15.
# Remove only those that no run can still be using: nothing in it written for an hour, and no java process now
# running started before its last write (a run makes its directory after it starts, and reads it until it ends).
(
  oldest=$(ps -C java -o etimes= 2>/dev/null | sort -n | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
  now=$(date +%s)
  find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'fortress*rats' -mmin +60 -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null |
  while read -r t d ; do
    [ -n "$oldest" ] && [ "${t%.*}" -ge $(( now - oldest )) ] && continue
    [ -n "$(find "$d" -newermt '60 minutes ago' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && continue
    rm -rf "$d"
  done
)

\hline
\EXP{\VAR{a}.\VAR{fill}(v\COLONOP{}E)} & {Initializes all elements with value \VAR{v}.} \\
\hline
\EXP{\VAR{a}.\VAR{tabulate}(f\COLONOP{}I\rightarrow{}E)} & {Calls \VAR{f} at each index and initializes the corresponding element with the result of the call.} \\
\hline
\EXP{\VAR{a}.\VAR{init}(i\COLONOP{}I, v\COLONOP{}E)} & {Initializes element at index \VAR{i} with value \VAR{v}.} \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\caption{\figlabel{arrayFactories}Factories for creating arrays and methods for initializing their elements}
\end{figure}
\revision{revival-tabulate}{The Working Draft of February 2011 gave the
method of \figref{arrayFactories} that calls \VAR{f} at each index the name
\VAR{fill}, which is also the name of the method above it that initializes
every element with one value.
When the element type \VAR{E} is \TYP{Any} or a function type, a function
is a value of type \VAR{E} as well as a function from \VAR{I} to \VAR{E},
and the two declarations are ambiguous; the method that calls \VAR{f} is
named \VAR{tabulate}, and \VAR{fill} keeps the value.}

\subsection{Initializing an array from a function}
\seclabel{revival-tabulate}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected section] \secref{arrays}.
\item[Change] In \figref{arrayFactories}, the method that calls a function at
each index and initializes the corresponding element with the result is named
\VAR{tabulate}; \VAR{fill} keeps the method that initializes every element with
one value.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; the revival decided
it on 26~September 2026.
The library declares the element type \VAR{E} of an array without a bound and
instantiates it at tuple types, which the implicit bound \TYP{Object} of
\secref{type-param} excludes; the interpreter reads such a parameter as bounded
by \TYP{Any}, and so does the compiled type checker when it checks the library.
\VAR{E} may then be \TYP{Any} or a function type, and a function passed to
\VAR{fill} is a value of type \VAR{E} as well as a function from \VAR{I} to
\VAR{E}: both declarations apply to the call and neither is more specific, which
the overloading rules forbid (\secref{incompatibility-rule}).
The compiled type checker refuses the pair; the interpreter chose between the two
by the argument's run-time type, so that on an array of element type \TYP{Any} a
function meant as the value was called at each index instead of being stored.
Where the library derived a second name, it gave it to a form that takes a
function (\VAR{ivmap} beside \VAR{map}); most languages that have both operations
name them differently, keeping \VAR{fill} for the value; and \VAR{tabulate} is
Scala's name for the other.
\item[Effect] A program initializes an array from a function with
\VAR{tabulate}. A call of \VAR{fill} with a function stores the function, on an
array whose element type admits it. The library's factories that build an array
from a function are renamed with the method; this specification does not list
them.
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/advanced/parallelism-locality/arrays-distributed.tex},
line 55, a row of the lower table of the figure:
\begin{quote}
\begin{tabular}{|m{2.0in}|m{3.4in}|}
\hline
\EXP{\VAR{a}.\VAR{fill}(f\COLONOP{}I\rightarrow{}E)} & {Calls \VAR{f} at each index and initializes the corresponding element with the result of the call.} \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{quote}
\item[Route C] The same under route~C.
contrast, the second set of libraries are the \emph{builtins}
(\secref{builtins}).  These libraries are intended to encompass
primitive functionality that must be visible in every Fortress
component.

- F-158 **`fill` takes a value and `tabulate` a function, both defined where the array diamond meets.** It builds P-89. `StandardMutableArrayType` and `ImmutableArray1`, the traits below both sides of the diamond, define them. A method declared only in each leaf leaves the meet refused by the checker's Meet Rule, so `copy` is declared on the meet too (row 467). Its factories are `tabulatedArray1` to `tabulatedArray3` and `tabulatedVector`. A demo still passes a function to `fill` (row 464). Gated by `tests/TabulateRungA.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-tabulate/REPORT.md` section 2.
- F-152 **`Vector` and `Matrix` are the only array traits with an algebra, `AdditiveGroup`, and their element must be a `Number`.** They inherit `+`, `-`, unary `-` and `zero`, and nothing from another algebraic trait. `Array3` has no algebra (row 292). `×` reaches no array, by design: juxtaposition is the inner product (rows 109, 293). Walk accepts, unchecked, a carrier that extends both `Matrix` and `MultiplicativeRing`, and its `+` then fails (row 371). The specification's `T^n` denotes these traits (row 24), and neither path takes it. Detail: `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 2.
- F-54 **The gate classes the distance to the switch-over by root cause, and the sized arrays and the one-off body errors lead.** The `#class` rows of each gate's `distance.txt` hold the counts. No coercion into an arbitrary `I extends Integral[\I\]` can be declared, so a numeral where such an `I` is expected needs `x.zero` or `x.one`. Row 680's crash hid no error: with its repair (F-233) the component's check finds none in `Array3`, and the distance lost its crash row. With `StandardMinMax[\T\]` added to the array bound, the overloading check ran past 15 minutes when measured, before row 688's memo. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage.md` sections 2 and 3.4; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-bounds/REPORT.md` section 6.
46:- F-53 **The distance to the switch-over is 31 errors and the checker count is 28, at the last landed gate.** The distance counts the checker's errors in the interpreter's library, led by the sized arrays (F-54). The count stops where the checker crashes or meets an error it cannot pass; since row 680's repair (F-233) nothing stops it, so its 28 are the `FortressLibrary` component's own errors, every api at 0. Both are reported, never red. By kind and by site, a rung's before (the `coordinator` skill, `references/batch.md`, "The checker count and the distance"): the last landed batch's `gate/distance.txt` and `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`.
54:- F-61 **"Use FortressLibrary for the compiler too" is three steps, of which the checker's sizes and the tower's errors are done and the natives are PLAN's phase 4.** F-67 and F-131 hold the first two. F-53 holds what the checker still reports on the library. F-32 counts the native bindings. No minimal `Array` or `Vector` shim can serve the compiler: `FlatArrays` uses the whole array protocol, `NativeArray.fss` and about 1,000 lines of the library. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md` section 5.

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

Matrices are indexed in the same manner as arrays.

A one-dimensional array whose elements are a subtype of \TYP{Number}
is a vector.
\marginnote{
can be coerced to a vector.
Vector types are written \EXP{\TYP{Vector}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket [n]}.
A type of this form can be abbreviated as

to be a physical dimension or unit.

A component must include, for every \apiN\ $A$ it exports,
matching definitions for all the declarations in $A$.
A matching definition of a declaration $d$
is a definition $d'$ with the same name as $d$
that includes definitions for all declarations
other than the methods or fields declared \KWD{abstract} in $d$.
The header and type of $d'$ must be the same as the header and type of $d$.

# Rung D (`rung-wrap-operators`): record lines for the gather

Written by the rung worker for the coordinator's fold. *At the gather of climb batch 5 (2026-09-26), where rung D did not land:* the judge's two wording corrections are made ("rung D's edit flips it", "varies with the JVM's flags"; `JUDGE.md` section 5, "Stated more strongly than measured"), nothing here is folded yet, and the provisional numbers 405-407 are not final: the ledger's rows 405-407 are rung S's, so these rows are numbered when D lands. `<D>` stands for the landed commit. Row numbers from 405 are provisional; the gather assigns the final numbers in manifest order (D, S, Z). The rung stopped on one output (section 6 of the report, `XXXInheritedOverload`), which holds the push until Pavol reads it. *At rung D's landing as a follow-up (2026-09-26):* `<D>` is `ab914b6e0`, and the provisional rows 405, 406 and 407 are the ledger's rows 427, 430 and 428. The "Landed semantics" entry and the handover line were folded in `896fae47c`; the notes for rows 403, 348 and 379, the sentence for the entry on fixed-width wrapping and the entry under "The harness and the gate" in the commit after `abe06a743`, the last with the judge's and row 430's wording where this text says more than was measured (the batch record, "Landed as a follow-up").

## FACTS.md

Under "Landed semantics", a new entry after "What relies on fixed-width wrapping under `walk`, and the wrapping operators no running library declares":

- **The specification's wrapping operators under `walk`** (2026-09-26, climb batch 5 rung D, `<D>`; `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/`; rows 348, 403). `DOTPLUS`, `DOTMINUS` (binary and unary) and `DOTTIMES`, the specification's ∔, ∸ and ⨰ (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:172-176`, `:205-209`), are declared abstract on `Integral[\I\]` and with bodies on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN64` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, `.fsi`) and `NN32` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, `.fsi`), each right after its plain operator, bound to wrapping natives of their own, `WrappingAdd`, `WrappingSub`, `WrappingMul` and `WrappingNegate` in `interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java`, `Long.java`, `NN32.java` and `UnsignedLong.java`, whose bodies are the old natives' bodies; on `ZZ` they are bound to the natives `+`, `-` and multiplication use, since on `ZZ` they "do exactly the same thing" (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:369-370`, `:400-401`, `:416`). The library bodies and the six team tests that meant to wrap are respelled with them, fully parenthesised (`Library/RangeInternals.fss`'s six splits, with the strided distance reordered on the checked operators; `Library/Random.fss:235`, `:241`; `Library/ChunkedSparseArray.fss:76`; `Library/IntMap.fss:675-676`; `ProjectFortress/tests/HeapTest.fss`, `intPrim.fss`, `longPrim.fss`, `QuickCheckTest.fss`, `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest.fss`, `UnsignedTest.fss`). Mixed without parentheses with `+`, `BITAND` or each other across the ⨰ boundary, they are refused before evaluation ("Loose operators ... have incomparable precedence"), as `Specification/appendices/operators.tex:27-29` requires; ∔ and ∸ mix left-associatively and ⨰ binds tighter (`:191`, `:213-224`). Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/WrapOperatorsRungD.fss`. `+`, `-` and multiplication still wrap under `walk` (row 379, batch 6's rung O), and the compiled prelude still spells the pair reversed (row 348's compiled half, at the switch-over). No interpreter test's output changed except by what Q2 = (a) normalises, save `XXXInheritedOverload`'s message order (row 406); the checker count stays 125.

Appended to the entry "What relies on fixed-width wrapping under `walk`, and the wrapping operators no running library declares": *Since rung D (`<D>`), the logging pass over `ProjectFortress/tests/`, the demos and the two microGPT checks meets an overflow in none of the eighteen natives except in `XXXFixedWidthOverflowRungB` (row 379's own test, by design), in `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest` through `QQ`'s `opr <`, which must not overflow and answers wrongly when its cross-products wrap (row 407), and in the demo `HeapShakedown` (row 405) (`compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/overflow-probe-summary-edit.txt`).*

Under "The harness and the gate", a new entry:

- **The interpreter's overload-ambiguity message names its two declarations in an order that is not a property of the program** (2026-09-26, climb batch 5 rung D; row 406). On the untouched tree at `6030e4b36`, `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXInheritedOverload.fss` under `walk` with the JVM's default flags names `a(x:Sub1,y:Base)` first in 11 of 16 runs and `a(x:Base,y:Sub2)` first in 5 (`compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/order/order-repeat-base.txt`); pinned to one core (`-XX:ActiveProcessorCount=1 -XX:+UseSerialGC -XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1`, the comparison runner's flags) it is fixed for a given library, and rung D's edit flips it. By reading, the order is that of a `GHashMap` keyed by the methods' signatures, whose hash comes from each `FType`'s global creation counter (`interpreter/evaluator/values/Constructor.java:181-182`, `:325-326`; `values/SingleFcn.java:87-95`; `evaluator/types/FType.java:88-101`). A three-pass output comparison with pinned flags therefore reports this file as stable and changed whenever the library gains declarations; the harness reads only that the `XXX` test fails.

## Ledger

- **Row 403**, appended to its notes, and closed for the sites it names: "Fixed `<D>` (climb batch 5, rung D): the sites it lists are respelled with ∔, ∸ and ⨰, or reordered (the strided distance), and the six team tests with them, every value unchanged (`compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/sites/SiteDifferential.txt`, 9,253 checks, 0 differ). The logging pass after the edit meets no overflow in the library sites or the tests this row lists (`compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/overflow-probe-summary-edit.txt`). What it still meets is not a wrap the code means: `QQ`'s `opr <` in `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest` (row 407), which the base pass also met (2,352 `Long$Mul` lines without the generator's multiplier, hidden among `LinearCongruential`'s), and row 379's own test. So the count rung O measures is predicted zero except `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest`, which depends on row 407 and on its random data."
- **Row 348**, appended: "Interpreter half fixed `<D>` (climb batch 5, rung D): the one library declares `DOTPLUS`, `DOTMINUS` and `DOTTIMES` with the specification's meaning, bound to wrapping natives (`ProjectFortress/tests/WrapOperatorsRungD.fss`); `walk` no longer says `Operator ? is not defined` for them (`compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/failure-preedit.txt` before, `probes/pass-postedit.txt` after). The compiled half, the prelude's reversed spellings in 10 compiled test files, closes at the switch-over; `XXXBoxDotSpellingsRungW` stays its expected failure."
- **Row 379**, appended: "Climb batch 5, rung D (`<D>`): the wrapping operators are declared and the library and tests respelled (rows 348, 403); the ten natives are unchanged, and `XXXFixedWidthOverflowRungB` still fails as expected (identical output in all three passes). Before rung O checks the natives: `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest` still meets an overflowing `Long$Mul` through `QQ`'s comparison (row 407), and the demo `HeapShakedown` through its `spread` (row 405); and an output comparison of rung O will meet row 406's order change only if rung O adds library declarations."
- **New row 405 (provisional)**: | 405 | **the demo `ProjectFortress/demos/HeapShakedown.fss` relies on `ZZ32` wrapping under `walk`**: its `spread` (`:114-118`) computes `c1 n + c2` with `c1 = -761155213`, the same scramble modulo 2^32 as `ProjectFortress/tests/HeapTest.fss:95-99` before rung D; under the logging shadow its whole run (34 s on the base, 30 s after the edit) meets 1,068 overflowing `Int$Add` and 10,872 `Int$Mul`, before and after rung D | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug (a program against the specification) | `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-155`, `:195-196` (integer overflow throws `IntegerOverflow`); wraparound has its own spelling, `:172-176`, `:205-209` | `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/overflow-probe-summary-base.txt` and `probes/overflow-probe-summary-edit.txt` (the logging pass; `probes/overflow-probe.patch`) | ours (climb batch 5, rung D's logging pass, 2026-09-26) | After batch 6's rung O the demo stops with `IntegerOverflow` under `ant testDemos` (outside the gate, `coordinator/map/test-coverage.md:26`, `:228`). Fix: respell `spread` as rung D respelled `HeapTest.fss:98`, `((c1 DOTTIMES n) DOTPLUS c2, n)`. No gated home in rung D: the demo and a second new test file were both outside its files; the demos run in no gated suite. For Pavol: whether rung O carries it. |
- **New row 406 (provisional)**: | 406 | **under `walk`, the ambiguity message of the overloading check names its two declarations in an order that varies with the JVM's flags and the library's contents**: `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXInheritedOverload.fss` on the untouched tree at `6030e4b36` names `a(x:Sub1,y:Base)` first in 11 of 16 runs and `a(x:Base,y:Sub2)` first in 5 with default JVM flags; pinned to one core the order is fixed per library, and rung D's edit flips it | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED (the variation); the mechanism by reading | interpreter quirk | none: the specification does not prescribe the text of a static error (`grep -rn 'fails because' Specification/basic/ Specification/basic-lib/` finds nothing), so home 3 | `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/order/order-repeat-base.txt`, `order-probe-base.txt`, `order-probe-base-passflags.txt`, `order-probe-base-passflags-fn.txt`, `order-probe.sh`; rung D's three passes, `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/count/XXXInheritedOverload.{baseA,edit,baseB}.txt` | ours (climb batch 5, rung D, 2026-09-26) | By reading: `Constructor` iterates a `GHashMap` keyed by each method signature (`interpreter/evaluator/values/Constructor.java:181-182`, `:325-326`) hashed from the domain `FType`s (`values/SingleFcn.java:87-95`), whose hash mixes a global creation counter (`evaluator/types/FType.java:88-101`); the pair check reports in that order (`values/OverloadedFunction.java:229-251`, `:555`). Adding 1 to 8 unrelated private traits or functions under pinned flags did not flip it, so which additions move the counter was not isolated. It makes a pinned three-pass comparison report a changed output when a rung adds library declarations (rung D's stop). A fix, if wanted, orders the pair by source position before reporting. |
- **New row 407 (provisional)**: | 407 | **under `walk`, `QQ`'s `opr <` compares two rationals by cross-multiplying their numerators and denominators in whatever width they hold, so with fixed-width parts the products wrap and the answer is wrong**: `(widen(1) LSHIFT 62) < 1/4` is `true` and `CMP` says `LessThan`; `(widen(1) LSHIFT 61)/3 < 5/7` is `true` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug | "Rational computations do not overflow" (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:156`, `:197`); `numerator` and `denominator` are declared `ZZ` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:378-379`), so the specification's products are unbounded | `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/rational/RationalCompareWrap.fss` with `RationalCompareWrap.txt` (walk) and `RationalCompareWrap-compiled.txt` (the compiled prelude has no `QQ`: "QQ is undefined"); in the test corpus, `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest`'s `propDoubleReversalMap` reaches it with random keys: `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/probes/rational/ReflectiveQuickCheckTest-raising-LongMul.txt` (with `long-mul-raising.patch`, the first overflowing `Long$Mul` is at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:540:44-46`) | ours (climb batch 5, rung D's logging pass, 2026-09-26) | The site is `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:537-541` (`(b=0 AND d=0 AND a=-1 AND c=1) OR (a d < b c)`), untouched by rung D. A `ZZ64` value's `numerator` is itself, a `Long` (row 146's shape: declared `ZZ`, held fixed-width). After batch 6's rung O the wrong answer becomes an `IntegerOverflow` in `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest` on runs whose random data reach it. Fix: compute the cross-products exactly, e.g. `big(a) big(d) < big(b) big(c)`, in the one library. Home 2 is owed (an `XXX` walk test asserting `(widen(1) LSHIFT 62) < 1/4` is `false`); rung D could not add it, being limited to one new test file. |

## Handover state line

Climb batch 5, rung D (the wrapping operators) landed on `wip/rung-wrap-operators`: ∔, ∸ and ⨰ declared on `Integral` and the five integer types of the one library with wrapping natives of their own, the library and six team tests respelled, `WrapOperatorsRungD` passing, 383 of 406 interpreter outputs identical and 5 normalised; stopped for Pavol on one output, `XXXInheritedOverload`'s message order, which already varies on its own under default JVM flags (row 406); the logging pass leaves `QQ`'s comparison (row 407) and the demo `HeapShakedown` (row 405) for rung O; checker count 125; rows 403 and 348's interpreter half closed.

## Revival changes, for the skill writer

Each landed rung's "Revival change" section, both its parts word for word, in the order the rungs landed, with the rows' numbers in place of the placeholders (rung S's two headings set one level down). Where a line it cites moved on `main`, the line on `main` follows the copy; then the skill sentences the rung's report lists as made false, which the batch does not edit.

### P (`rung-existential-reduction`, `14e91723f`)

**The change.**
- The team's sources: the team's compiled checker read two declarations as excluding each other only where its subtyping showed their meet below Bottom, `sa.subtypeED(md, BOTTOM)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala:190-195` at `a874948ac`), and its existential reduction gives up where the constraint that the meet is not Bottom is False, `unifyWithDebug(c, debug).getOrElse(return None)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:404` at `a874948ac`), leaving the meet as it was. So it refused `copyOf[\T\](a: Thawed[\T\])` beside `copyOf[\T\](a: Frozen[\T\])`, where `Frozen[\E\]` and `Thawed[\E\]` extend `Readable[\E\]` and exclude each other, and `o[\T\](x: P[\T\], b: Box[\T\])` beside `o[\T\](x: Q[\T\], b: Box[\T\])`, where `P[\T\] excludes { Q[\T\] }` and `Box` is an object: 'Invalid overloading of copyOf', 'Invalid overloading of o'. The team's walk loaded two generic declarations only where some one pair of their parameter types excluded each other (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:496-498`, message `:527`, at `a874948ac`); it read no exclusion across positions.
- What the tree now does: both paths read the whole parameter type. Two declarations, one or both with static parameters, exclude where a value of both would need instances of one generic type at static arguments that cannot be equal, at one position or across positions, the static argument that one parameter forces holding at the others; the compiled checker reads this through the instance of a supertype the parameter types share. The `o` pair, the same with renamed static parameters, through a supertype, over sizes, and a pair whose forced static argument would be two types, beside a generic or a plain declaration, load and dispatch under walk (`ProjectFortress/tests/GenericPairExcludesTogetherWalk`) and compile and dispatch (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/GenericPairExcludesTogether`, `GenericPairSharedSupertypeExclusion`). A pair whose second declaration leaves the forced static argument free is still refused on both paths (`ProjectFortress/tests/GenericPairFreeArgumentWalk`, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXGenericPairFreeArgument`). Two type parameters whose bounds exclude, `tint[\T extends Red\]` beside `tint[\T extends Blue\]` over `Box[\T\]`, still load under walk and are refused by the checker. Walk reads, at the static arguments the other positions force, an object type apart from a type that neither it nor a supertype of it may be, so `k[\T\](x: T, b: Box[\T\])` beside `k[\U\](x: Q[\U\], b: Box[\Lone\])` loads, `Lone` an object type that is no `Q` (`ProjectFortress/tests/GenericPairForcedObjectApartWalk`), and `h[\T\](x: Box[\T\], y: T)` beside `h[\U\](x: Box[\Ob[\U\]\], y: R[\U\])`, `Ob[\U\]` extending `R[\ZZ32\]`, is refused (`ProjectFortress/tests/GenericPairObjectSupertypeOverlapWalk`); a pair one of whose declarations has a `where` clause is still refused under walk (row 787).
- The reason: the type group's paper of 2011 reads the intersection of two domains that exclude as having "the same extent as \Bottom", so that the Meet Rule holds for them by the implicit declaration on Bottom (`Papers/Types/exc-reduction.tick:7-21`; `Papers/Types/rules.tick:205-219`), gathers the constraint over the whole type, a tuple element by element (`Papers/Types/fig-exclusion.tick:55-57`) and every pair of ancestors (`:136-147`); its figure's `unify` has no solution for a False constraint, so the figure leaves the case that its prose decides (`Papers/Types/exc-reduction.tick:62-73`). The specification reads exclusion by that reduction (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex`, "Declarations with Static Parameters"). Measured on the code before: 'Invalid overloading of copyOf', of `o`, `r`, `viaR`, `pairOf` and `plainOf` (`compiler_tests` run, 'Tests run: 7, Failures: 6'), and under walk 'Overloading of o[\T\](x:Q[\T\],b:Box[\T\]) ... and o[\T\](x:P[\T\],b:Box[\T\])' refused at load.

**Provenance.** P-152 (exclusion between two generic declarations read over the whole parameter type, on both paths), with P-45 and P-26; the batch record's section 2, forks 1 to 9, at their defaults: one rung for both paths, walk's branch beside a plain declaration, `tint` kept on both paths with a row of its own (the probe's question 1, default), the checker's change local to its exclusion test with the bounds left out, P-148's pass where the profile shows the added code, `overloading.tex`'s passage revised; the P-152 probe, `explorations/perf-probes/existential-reduction/` (`walk.patch`, `checker.patch`); climb batch 19, rung P.

Sentences this makes false, for the writer and the gather:
- `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:58`, the bullet "walk and the checker refuse a pair whose parameter types exclude only together ... (ledger row 740)": both now load or compile it.
- `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:61`, the bullet's first half, "the checker refuses ... two generic traits that exclude each other and extend one shared generic trait, as `copyOf` ...": the checker now accepts it; its second half, `tint`, stays true, now row 786 and no longer row 741.
- `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:56`, "In seven cases": six stay, `tint` among them as its own case.

Lines on `main`: the change cites the team's tree at `a874948ac`, the landed tests and the specification by section; `OverloadedFunction.java`, `OverloadingOracle.scala` and `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala` are rung P's alone on `main`, so its lines stand. One citation of the team's tree is a line early: walk's old check, `OverloadedFunction.java:496-498` at `a874948ac` in the copy, is `:497-499` there, its comment "non-ground types need exclusion" at `:497` and the refusal `if (sawSymbolic1 || sawSymbolic2 || unrelated != -1)` at `:498-499`, as rung P's skeptic read it (`SKEPTIC.md` section 6; the merged-diff review). Skill sentences made false, from the rung's `REPORT.md` section 8 and its skeptic's `leftForGather`: `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:58` (row 740's bullet, now false: both paths load or compile the pair), `:61` (its `copyOf` half, now false; its `tint` half stays, now row 786 and no longer row 741) and `:56` ("In seven cases": six stay, `tint` among them as its own case).

### S (`rung-string-conversion`, `4190069c4`)

#### The change

1. **An object or trait declared `extends Any`.**
   - The team's source: the pre-disambiguation desugaring gives an empty `extends` clause `{Object}` and leaves every other clause as written (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/desugarer/PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:62-72` at `612869b4a`). So under walk and compiled, an object or trait declared `extends Any` was not an `Object`: `typecase` took the `else` arm, and an object with no `asString` of its own had none ("Cannot find definition for method asString given receiver Inf"). The team's own test of such an object says "We ought to be able to extend the builtin type Any." (`ProjectFortress/tests/extendAny.fss:16`).
   - What the tree now does: a clause each of whose types is `Any` gets `{Object}` too, except in the declarations of `Any` and `Object` themselves (`PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:59-68`, `:76`, `:123-124`). Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/ExtendsAnyIsObjectWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExtendsAnyIsObject.test`.
   - The reason: "every trait except Any and Object implicitly extends the trait Object if it does not do so explicitly" (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:186-188`); `Object` "is the root of the type hierarchy for all user-constructed objects" (`Specification/basic-lib/objects.tex:131-132`); "Any comprises of tuple types, arrow types, (), and Object" (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:153`).
2. **`String`'s concatenation with a value of any type.**
   - The team's library: `opr ||(a:Any, self):String = a.asString || self` and `opr ||(self, b:Any):String = self || b.asString` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4393-4394` at `612869b4a`), which call a method of `Object` on an `Any`. Walk stopped with `ProgramError` "Non-object receiver (1,2): (Int,Int) trying to invoke method asString" for a tuple or `()` on the left of a string, and the compiled checker refuses both bodies: "Any has no getter called asString".
   - What the tree now does: `("" || a) || self` and `self || cast[\Object\](b).asString`. A tuple or `()` on the left of a string concatenates as on the right, and a function or a tuple of seven or more elements beside a string raises `CastError` where it raised `ProgramError`. Test: `ProjectFortress/tests/ConcatAnyOnLeftWalk.fss`; the checker no longer reports either body.
   - The reason: the library's own comment on `print(a:Any) = print("" a)`, "These use concatenation rather than .asString because the formulation with concat also works for tuples" (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4494-4495`); the checker's refusal above.
3. **`FlatString`'s api.**
   - The team's api: `object FlatString extends { String }` with `opr ||(a:FlatString, self): String` (`Library/FlatString.fsi:16`, `:20` at `612869b4a`), where its component extends `{ String, DelegatedIndexed[\Char, ZZ32\] }` and declares no such member (`Library/FlatString.fss:34`).
   - What the tree now does: the api has the component's header and drops the member (`Library/FlatString.fsi:16-21`). Test: the checker's export check reports no mismatch for `FlatString`.
   - The reason: the checker's export error, "The following declarations in API FlatString are not matched by the declarations in component FlatString ... due to different extends clauses ... different method ||".

#### Provenance

- F-246 (the conversion, the probe's way C, and FlatString's two lines).
- PLAN's phase 3, item 17: the `String` sites taken with row 743 repaired beside, which answers the symbolic-operators probe's question (c).
- Climb batch 19's forks 10 to 14 (the conversion alone; the repair in the pre-disambiguation desugaring; walk's moved values as the conversion gives them; FlatString's two api lines; no speed pass).
- Rows 743 (closed), 726, 585, 374 and 369 (noted).
- Climb batch 19, rung S.

Lines on `main`: the change cites the base `612869b4a` and the landed library, desugaring and tests, whose lines are rung S's alone; they stand. Skill sentences made false: none listed by the rung's report, whose section 8 lists record sentences only; the skill's part on revival changes gains this change.

# Rung A: the array sites by the library's own devices, with decision E's diff

- problem: the distance's 19 array sites and its first export error, climb batch 19's per-site list, `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv:2`, `:4-5`, `:13-27`, `:29`, `:31` (31 at that gate, `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-19/gate/distance.txt:2`), measured 31 to 11 by the array probe (`explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/REPORT.md:6-16`)
- spec: no passage of `Specification/basic` or `basic-lib` names these declarations (`grep -rn 'immutableArray\|array3\|tabulatedVector\|__builtinFactory\|__immutableFactory\|pmul\|rmul\|lmul' Specification --include=*.tex | grep -v library/apis/` prints none of them); beside them, a one-dimensional array of numbers "is a vector" and one of two dimensions "is a matrix", `Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:152-155`, `:165-166`, and a matching definition's "header and type ... must be the same as the header and type of d", `Specification/basic/components/apis.tex:249-256`
- precedent: `ImmutableArray1`'s leaf `fill` and `tabulate` at its own type, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2407-2414`, `.fsi:1580-1581`; `array1`'s arms returning through the library's `cast`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2585-2592` (row 685's fix); the component's own headers of the vector and matrix products, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2611-2627`, `:3008-3031`
- deviation: none from the two patches, which are applied unchanged (`git apply` of `explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/ways.patch`, then `e3-rebased.patch`, no fuzz): `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2525-2540`
- deviation: the leaf `fill` and `tabulate` open `Vector` and `Matrix` in the component and close them in the api, where `ImmutableArray1` puts them mid-trait in both (form only, the probe's): `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1624-1625`, `:1746-1747`
- deviation: the guard asserts a column's and a row's type and size, not their elements, on an `Array2` based above zero, where the brief asks for the elements, because the base reads them at the wrong offset (new row NEW-A-1, section 9): `ProjectFortress/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss:136-141`
- historical: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2522-2535`, `:2551-2568`, `:2697`, `:2701`, `:2835-2914`, `:2945-2950`, `:2976-2977`; `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1499-1501`, `:1613-1622`, `:1649-1677`, `:1731-1742`, `:1774-1804`, `:1860` (lines at the base `97ccd5f1f`)

## 1. What changed and why

Two commits on `wip/rung-array-sites`: the tests, `73e47c30d`; the library, `48d809df2`, which is `ways.patch` and then `e3-rebased.patch` applied as they are (`git apply`, no fuzz; `git apply --check -R` of `e3-rebased.patch` on the result passes).

The compiled checker, run over the interpreter's library, refused 19 bodies of the array code and reported 17 api declarations that the component lacks. Each fix is a device the library already uses for the same kind of thing (P-27):

- **1a, the leaf `fill` and `tabulate`.** `Vector` and `Matrix` declare `fill(v:T)` and `tabulate(f)` at their own type, with `StandardMutableArrayType`'s two bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2525-2532`, `:2846-2853`; api `.fsi:1624-1625`, `:1746-1747`), as `ImmutableArray1` does at its own. So `vector(v)`, `tabulatedVector`, `rmul` and `lmul`, which build through `vector[\T,s0\]().fill` or `.tabulate`, answer a `Vector` (`:2604`, `:2606`, `:2922`, `:2927`), and `matrix(v)` builds through `matrix[\T,s0,s1\]()` where it called `array2[\T,s0,s1\]()` (`:2993`). Five sites.
- **1c, the library's `cast`** (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-37`) around `Vector`'s `+`, binary and unary `-`, `scale` and `pmul` (`:2534-2540`) and `Matrix`'s `+`, binary and unary `-` and `scale` (`:2855-2859`), whose bodies call the parent's `map` and `ivmap`, typed `Array1` and `Array2`. Nine sites.
- **2a, a `cast` in the size-tested arm:** the `N[\0\]` arm of `__builtinFactory1` and `__immutableFactory1` (`:2562`, `:2573`) and `__builtinFactory2`'s first branch (`:2963`). Three sites.
- **3d, `Col` and `Row`** take `cast[\Array2[\T,0,s0,0,1\]\](self[(b0,i1)#(s0,1)])` and `cast[\Array2[\T,0,1,0,s1\]\](self[(i0,b1)#(1,s1)])` (`:2705`, `:2709`): the range subscript answers the unsized `Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]`, and its value is a 0-based sized `Array2` (`:2676-2683`). Two sites; row 678's own.
- **4d, `immutableArray`'s ranks 2 and 3** inside `(* ... *)` in the api (`.fsi:1500-1503`), as the component has had them since the team's last commit (`.fss:2264-2280`; `a874948ac` `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1941-1952`). No `ImmutableArray2` or `ImmutableArray3` exists. Two entries of the first export error.
- **4f, `array3[\T, nat s0, nat s1, nat s2\](v:T):Array3[\T,0,s0,0,s1,0,s2\]`** declared in the api (`.fsi:1867`), as `array1(v)` and `array2(v)` are; the component has it (`.fss:3199`). One entry.
- **E3, decision E's diff (P-40):** the api's 17 vector and matrix operators lose their unused sizes (`.fsi:1653-1680`, `:1780-1802`): the vector `+`, binary and unary `-` drop `nat m`; the six vector `DOT` and juxtaposition forms drop `nat m, nat p`; the eight matrix-vector, vector-matrix and scalar forms drop `nat p`. The matrix `+` and `-`, which use their `m`, keep it (`.fsi:1763-1770`). The component's headers already had the shorter form (`.fss:2611-2627`, `:3008-3031`). Fourteen entries; the three vector `+`/`-` lines were never entries.

## Revival change

### The change

- The team's sources: the library's api declared the vector and matrix products and the vector `+` and `-` with static sizes that occur in no parameter, result or body, as `opr DOT[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m, nat p \](me : Vector[\T,n\], other : Vector[\T,n\]):T`, where the component declares `[\T, nat n\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1495-1525`, `:1621-1645` at `a874948ac`); it declared `immutableArray`'s ranks 2 and 3 (`.fsi:1352-1353` at `a874948ac`), which the component had only in a comment (`.fss:1941-1952` at `a874948ac`), with no immutable array of rank 2 or 3 in the library; it declared `array3()` alone where the component also defines `array3(v)` (`.fsi:1701`, `.fss:2814-2818` at `a874948ac`). The component's `Vector` and `Matrix` answered their `+`, `-`, unary `-`, `scale` and `pmul` with the parent array's `map` or `ivmap`, typed `Array1` or `Array2`, under a declared `Vector` or `Matrix`, and so did `vector(v)`, `tabulatedVector`, `rmul`, `lmul` and `matrix(v)` through the parent's `fill` and `tabulate`; the size-tested arms of `__builtinFactory1` and `__builtinFactory2`, and `Col` and `Row`'s argument, had the same shape (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2189-2202`, `:2359`, `:2363` at `a874948ac`).
- What the tree now does: the api's operators carry only the sizes they use (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1653-1680`, `:1780-1802`); `immutableArray`'s ranks 2 and 3 are in a comment in the api too (`.fsi:1500-1503`); the api declares `array3[\T, nat s0, nat s1, nat s2\](v:T)` (`.fsi:1867`); `Vector` and `Matrix` declare `fill` and `tabulate` at their own type (`.fsi:1624-1625`, `:1746-1747`; `.fss:2525-2532`, `:2846-2853`); and their operations, the factories' base-0 arms and `Col` and `Row`'s argument return through the library's `cast` to the declared sized type (`.fss:2534-2540`, `:2855-2859`, `:2562`, `:2573`, `:2963`, `:2705`, `:2709`). Under walk every value is as before. Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss` (each operation's type and elements at the eight number types); the compiled checker, run over the library, reports none of these sites and no api declaration missing from the component.
- The reason: the compiled checker's refusals, "Function body has type Array1[\T,0,s0\], but declared return type is Vector[\T,s0\]." and its `Matrix` and factory-arm twins, "Could not check call to function Col ... is not applicable to an argument of type Array[\T,(ZZ32, ZZ32)\].", and "Component FortressLibrary exports API FortressLibrary but does not define all declarations in FortressLibrary. Missing declarations {...}" over the 14 products, `array3()` and the two ranks; and the specification's export rule, "The header and type of d' must be the same as the header and type of d" (`Specification/basic/components/apis.tex:249-256`). The `cast` and the leaf redeclaration are the library's own devices for a result's precise type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-37`, `:2407-2414`, `:2585-2592`).

- P-40: the unused sizes of the api's 17 vector and matrix operators by decision E's diff, which the curator read and took (ask 3, 2026-10-20; `explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/e3-rebased.patch`), built with the array sites' other fixes; F-35 for the sizes' history.

# Rung A: the array sites by the library's own devices, with decision E's diff

- problem: the distance's 19 array sites and its first export error, climb batch 19's per-site list, `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv:2`, `:4-5`, `:13-27`, `:29`, `:31` (31 at that gate, `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-19/gate/distance.txt:2`), measured 31 to 11 by the array probe (`explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/REPORT.md:6-16`)
- spec: no passage of `Specification/basic` or `basic-lib` names these declarations (`grep -rn 'immutableArray\|array3\|tabulatedVector\|__builtinFactory\|__immutableFactory\|pmul\|rmul\|lmul' Specification --include=*.tex | grep -v library/apis/` prints none of them); beside them, a one-dimensional array of numbers "is a vector" and one of two dimensions "is a matrix", `Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:152-155`, `:165-166`, and a matching definition's "header and type ... must be the same as the header and type of d", `Specification/basic/components/apis.tex:249-256`
- precedent: `ImmutableArray1`'s leaf `fill` and `tabulate` at its own type, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2407-2414`, `.fsi:1580-1581`; `array1`'s arms returning through the library's `cast`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2585-2592` (row 685's fix); the component's own headers of the vector and matrix products, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2611-2627`, `:3008-3031`
- deviation: none from the two patches, which are applied unchanged (`git apply` of `explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/ways.patch`, then `e3-rebased.patch`, no fuzz): `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2525-2540`
- deviation: the leaf `fill` and `tabulate` open `Vector` and `Matrix` in the component and close them in the api, where `ImmutableArray1` puts them mid-trait in both (form only, the probe's): `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1624-1625`, `:1746-1747`
- deviation: the guard asserts a column's and a row's type and size, not their elements, on an `Array2` based above zero, where the brief asks for the elements, because the base reads them at the wrong offset (new row NEW-A-1, section 9): `ProjectFortress/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss:136-141`
- historical: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2522-2535`, `:2551-2568`, `:2697`, `:2701`, `:2835-2914`, `:2945-2950`, `:2976-2977`; `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1499-1501`, `:1613-1622`, `:1649-1677`, `:1731-1742`, `:1774-1804`, `:1860` (lines at the base `97ccd5f1f`)

## 1. What changed and why

Two commits on `wip/rung-array-sites`: the tests, `73e47c30d`; the library, `48d809df2`, which is `ways.patch` and then `e3-rebased.patch` applied as they are (`git apply`, no fuzz; `git apply --check -R` of `e3-rebased.patch` on the result passes).

The compiled checker, run over the interpreter's library, refused 19 bodies of the array code and reported 17 api declarations that the component lacks. Each fix is a device the library already uses for the same kind of thing (P-27):

- **1a, the leaf `fill` and `tabulate`.** `Vector` and `Matrix` declare `fill(v:T)` and `tabulate(f)` at their own type, with `StandardMutableArrayType`'s two bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2525-2532`, `:2846-2853`; api `.fsi:1624-1625`, `:1746-1747`), as `ImmutableArray1` does at its own. So `vector(v)`, `tabulatedVector`, `rmul` and `lmul`, which build through `vector[\T,s0\]().fill` or `.tabulate`, answer a `Vector` (`:2604`, `:2606`, `:2922`, `:2927`), and `matrix(v)` builds through `matrix[\T,s0,s1\]()` where it called `array2[\T,s0,s1\]()` (`:2993`). Five sites.
- **1c, the library's `cast`** (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-37`) around `Vector`'s `+`, binary and unary `-`, `scale` and `pmul` (`:2534-2540`) and `Matrix`'s `+`, binary and unary `-` and `scale` (`:2855-2859`), whose bodies call the parent's `map` and `ivmap`, typed `Array1` and `Array2`. Nine sites.
- **2a, a `cast` in the size-tested arm:** the `N[\0\]` arm of `__builtinFactory1` and `__immutableFactory1` (`:2562`, `:2573`) and `__builtinFactory2`'s first branch (`:2963`). Three sites.
- **3d, `Col` and `Row`** take `cast[\Array2[\T,0,s0,0,1\]\](self[(b0,i1)#(s0,1)])` and `cast[\Array2[\T,0,1,0,s1\]\](self[(i0,b1)#(1,s1)])` (`:2705`, `:2709`): the range subscript answers the unsized `Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]`, and its value is a 0-based sized `Array2` (`:2676-2683`). Two sites; row 678's own.
- **4d, `immutableArray`'s ranks 2 and 3** inside `(* ... *)` in the api (`.fsi:1500-1503`), as the component has had them since the team's last commit (`.fss:2264-2280`; `a874948ac` `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1941-1952`). No `ImmutableArray2` or `ImmutableArray3` exists. Two entries of the first export error.
- **4f, `array3[\T, nat s0, nat s1, nat s2\](v:T):Array3[\T,0,s0,0,s1,0,s2\]`** declared in the api (`.fsi:1867`), as `array1(v)` and `array2(v)` are; the component has it (`.fss:3199`). One entry.
- **E3, decision E's diff (P-40):** the api's 17 vector and matrix operators lose their unused sizes (`.fsi:1653-1680`, `:1780-1802`): the vector `+`, binary and unary `-` drop `nat m`; the six vector `DOT` and juxtaposition forms drop `nat m, nat p`; the eight matrix-vector, vector-matrix and scalar forms drop `nat p`. The matrix `+` and `-`, which use their `m`, keep it (`.fsi:1763-1770`). The component's headers already had the shorter form (`.fss:2611-2627`, `:3008-3031`). Fourteen entries; the three vector `+`/`-` lines were never entries.

## 2. The failing runs and the passing runs

**The library's sites: the distance stage.** Its before is climb batch 19's landed tables, not run again (POSITIONS.md, "No re-measuring what the record holds."):

The after, on the final tree `48d809df2` (started 2026-10-20T07:23:55Z):

**The guard, `ProjectFortress/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss`.** A guard of a behaviour that holds today, so it has no failing run: it passes on the base and after.

    $ explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-array-sites/h-guard ProjectFortress/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss
    # harness-one 2026-10-20T07:16:32Z; tree 97ccd5f1f; nproc=4; load 0.95 0.73 0.58; openjdk version "25.0.4.1" 2026-08-18; FORTRESS_THREADS=4; cache filled
    . interpret tmp/rung-array-sites/h-guard/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk
    PASS

and, after the edit, in the run of the 42 files of section 5 (`# harness-one 2026-10-20T07:20:21Z; tree 73e47c30d`, the library edit in the working tree, committed unchanged as `48d809df2`):

    . interpret tmp/rung-array-sites/h-walk-new/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk
    PASS
     OK (time = 1444ms)
    OK (42 tests)

At each of `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR32` and `RR64`, through generic helpers called with the type written (`vectorOps[\T\]`, `matrixOps[\T\]`, `slices[\T\]`, `factories[\T\]`), it asserts the type and the elements of: `Vector`'s `+`, binary and unary `-`, `scale`, `pmul`, `fill` and `tabulate`; `Matrix`'s the same, with `rmul` and `lmul`; `vector(v)`, `tabulatedVector` and `matrix(v)` (diagonal and zero); a transposed matrix and its `+`; `a[:, j]` and `a[i, :]` of a matrix; both arms of `__builtinFactory1`, called at base 0 and 1 and reached through `map` of a 0-based column and of a 1-based subarray; both arms of `__immutableFactory1`; and `__builtinFactory2` at base (0,0) and (1,1), with a column and a row of the latter. The values: 5, 2 and 3 at the five integer types (by `widen`, `unsigned` and `big`), 5/2, 1/2 and 3/4 at `QQ`, 5.0, 2.0 and 0.75 at `RR32` (by `narrow`), 2.5, 0.5 and 0.75 at `RR64`; each type holds each value exactly, and every sum, difference and product the helpers form. The unsigned types meet unary minus on an array of zeros: an unsigned type negates only zero (a nonzero one raises `IntegerOverflow` in the element's own `-`, inside `map`, before any cast), so the vector's and the matrix's unary minus are asserted at `NN32` and `NN64` on `fill(0)`.

## 3. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent

- **The place.** The library: the bodies, factories and api declarations the checker refuses are in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, walk's library, which the compiled path will check at the switch-over (the map's arrays row, `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:329`: library `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, compiler prelude "absent"). No checker change clears them: `Array1[\T,0,s0\]` is a supertype of `Vector[\T,s0\]`, and a rule that accepted it as `Vector` would accept a non-vector array (the ways note, section 1, way 6).
- **The ways the language and the library offer**, each with its evidence in the ways note (`explorations/reviews/array-sites-ways.md`, sections 1 to 5): for the 14 bodies, 1a the leaf redeclaration, 1b the bodies through the factory's `tabulate`, 1c the `cast`, 1d `map` overloaded at the element type, 1e a self type on the leaves; for the 3 arms, 2a the `cast`, 2b a checker that refines a size in the arm, 2c overloading on the witness, 2d no branch, 2e an `if` that refines; for `Col` and `Row`, 3a a `SubArray2` at the run-time offset, 3b the receiver's `subarray` with the offset opened, 3c `Col` and `Row` over the unsized array, 3d the `cast`, 3e a sized subscript result; for the first export error, 4a decision E's diff, 4b the component carrying the unused sizes, 4c an export check that ignores them, 4d the two ranks commented out, 4e the two ranks built, 4f `array3(v)` declared. The rung builds 1a with 1c, 2a, 3d, 4a, 4d and 4f: the batch record's forks 4 to 6 and P-40.
- **The precedents and their sites.** The `cast` that gives a factory's result its sized type is row 685's fix (`a0f839ad7`): at the base the component calls `cast` 38 times (39 lines with its declaration at `:33`: `array1`'s 8 arms, `array2`'s 8, `additiveIdentity`'s 18, `openRange`'s 3 and one at `:4394`), and after this rung 52 (53 lines: 9 bodies, 3 arms, `Col` and `Row`). The leaf `fill` and `tabulate` had one precedent, `ImmutableArray1` (`f3b62bc83`); with this rung three leaves declare them. Of the defect these precedents repaired, a sized array's body or factory typed by an unsized or parent type (the distance's class V2, and `Col` and `Row` in class OT), no site remains in the distance (section 4).

## 4. The checker count and the distance

Neither stage was run on the base (POSITIONS.md, "No re-measuring what the record holds."): the before is climb batch 19's gate, `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-19/gate/checker-count.txt` and `distance.txt`, and the per-site list `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`. # Rung A (`rung-array-sites`): record lines for the gather

Written by the rung worker of climb batch 20 for the gather's fold. `<A>` stands for the landed commit of `48d809df2` (the library) with `73e47c30d` (the tests). NEW-A-1 is the placeholder of the one new row.

## FACTS.md

Under "The library's arrays and algebra", in place of F-260's measurement:

- **The array code's 19 typecheck sites and the api's first export error are gone: `Vector` and `Matrix` redeclare `fill` and `tabulate` at their own type, the library's `cast` types their parent-typed bodies, the size-tested factory arms and `Col`'s and `Row`'s subscript value, and the api drops its 17 operators' unused sizes.** The api also puts `immutableArray`'s ranks 2 and 3 in a comment, as the component has them, and declares `array3(v)`. The distance goes 31 to 11 and the count 28 to 9, nothing come; the second export error's 44 entries stay. Under walk no value moves: each cast holds at the eight number types, on a transposed matrix, and through both arms of the 1-D and 2-D factories. Test: `ProjectFortress/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss`, and the distance stage. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-array-sites/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 4.

F-35's sentences "The `FortressLibrary` api has 25 declarations with a dead size" (now 8) and "Six vector `DOT` and juxtaposition operators have this shape ... and give one of the distance's export errors (F-53)" (the api has the component's shape, and the error is gone) are false after `<A>`; F-54's "the sized arrays ... lead" (class V2 is 0), F-58's "3 `DOT` calls that fail on the api's unused sizes" (by reading cleared, not measured) and F-158's "both defined where the array diamond meets" (two leaves declare them too) need the same reading (REPORT.md section 7).

## Ledger

- **Row 678**, closed: `close 678 --commit <A> --test VectorMatrixCastsWalk`, with: "`Col(cast[\Array2[\T,0,s0,0,1\]\](self[(b0,i1)#(s0,1)]))` and `Row(cast[\Array2[\T,0,1,0,s1\]\](self[(i0,b1)#(1,s1)]))`, the row's third way (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2705`, `:2709` at `48d809df2`); the distance's two sites gone on the rung's tree (31 to 11); `VectorMatrixCastsWalk` asserts a matrix's column and row at the eight number types, and at an `Array2` based at (1,1) their type and size."
- **Row 465**, appended to its notes: "Climb batch 20, rung A (`<A>`): the api now declares `array3[\T, nat s0, nat s1, nat s2\](v:T)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1867`), so the row's example is a declared call, and it runs (`array3(v) 5 true`). The claim stands: walk resolving an overload the api does not declare beside one it does. A line scan of `FortressLibrary`'s top-level declarations finds no other name the component overloads beyond the api; no other example met."
- **New row NEW-A-1**, in section 9, "Arrays, vectors and matrices":

| NEW-A-1 | under walk, a column `a[:, j]`, a row `a[i, :]` or a range subscript of an `Array2` based above zero reads the wrong elements: on a 2 by 3 array based at (1,1), `(a[:,1])[0]` is `a[2,2]`, and the column's next element raises Java's `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug (library) | `basic/expressions/ranges.tex`, "Ranges" | `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXArray2SliceAtNonzeroBase.fss` | climb batch 20 rung A | `Array2.subarray` hands `SubArray2`, whose offsets are 0-based, the subscript's offset in the array's own index space, with no `- b0` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2727-2731`, `:2795` at 48d809df2), where `Array1.subarray` subtracts it (`:2454-2457`); both the team's. `Array3.subarray` has the same shape (`:3128-3133`), not measured. 0-based arrays and matrices are unaffected. ## Handover line

Climb batch 20, rung A (the array sites) on `wip/rung-array-sites`: `ways.patch` and `e3-rebased.patch` applied unchanged, the distance 31 to 11 and the count 28 to 9 with nothing come, the count stage 67 s; `VectorMatrixCastsWalk` passing on the base and after, walk's 40 array tests, `ant testSystem` (666), `ant testSpecData` (130) and microGPT's quick pair unchanged; row 678 to close, row 465 noted, one new row (NEW-A-1, `XXXArray2SliceAtNonzeroBase`).

## Revival change

### The change

- The team's sources: the library's api declared the vector and matrix products and the vector `+` and `-` with static sizes that occur in no parameter, result or body, as `opr DOT[\ T extends Number, nat n, nat m, nat p \](me : Vector[\T,n\], other : Vector[\T,n\]):T`, where the component declares `[\T, nat n\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1495-1525`, `:1621-1645` at `a874948ac`); it declared `immutableArray`'s ranks 2 and 3 (`.fsi:1352-1353` at `a874948ac`), which the component had only in a comment (`.fss:1941-1952` at `a874948ac`), with no immutable array of rank 2 or 3 in the library; it declared `array3()` alone where the component also defines `array3(v)` (`.fsi:1701`, `.fss:2814-2818` at `a874948ac`). Under walk every value is as before. Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss` (each operation's type and elements at the eight number types); the compiled checker, run over the library, reports none of these sites and no api declaration missing from the component.

Missing declarations {...}" over the 14 products, `array3()` and the two ranks; and the specification's export rule, "The header and type of d' must be the same as the header and type of d" (`Specification/basic/components/apis.tex:249-256`). The `cast` and the leaf redeclaration are the library's own devices for a result's precise type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-37`, `:2407-2414`, `:2585-2592`).

### Provenance

- P-40: the unused sizes of the api's 17 vector and matrix operators by decision E's diff, which the curator read and took (ask 3, 2026-10-20; `explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/e3-rebased.patch`), built with the array sites' other fixes; F-35 for the sizes' history.
